# Behaviour profiles

<!-- Generated by scripts/behaviour-profiles.py from
     src/peer_connection/configuration/behaviour_profile.rs. Do not edit by hand. -->

**50 governed behaviours.** Chrome values: **12 observed**, **38 from libwebrtc's source**, **0 unverified**. **12 not expressible.**

A `BehaviourProfile` sets, in one call, every default where the engine and an RFC, or the
engine and libwebrtc (Chrome), choose differently:

- **`Rfc`**: the engine's defaults, unchanged. The RFCs' behaviour, and the interoperable
  form where a named browser or deployed peer cannot take the RFC's (the audit's `setting`
  verdict, `docs/conformance/audit/RULES.md`).
- **`Chrome`**: libwebrtc's choice wherever the engine and libwebrtc both do a thing and
  choose differently (a timer, an order, a form on the wire, a lenient or strict acceptance
  rule). It never turns off a capability the engine has and Chrome lacks: those are the same
  in every profile (section 2), so the `Chrome` profile's offers are a **superset** of
  Chrome's (extra header extensions, `a=rtcp-fb` types, `a=tls-id`, formats).
- **`StrictRfc`**: the RFC form even where the default is the interoperable one. For
  conformance testing only: **it does not interoperate with browsers** (Chromium, Firefox
  and WebKit refuse an answer whose bundled sections lack `a=rtcp-mux`; a data-only
  association without `use_srtp` cannot gain media with a browser).
- **`Performance`**: the engine's defaults, with each behaviour where an RFC offers a form
  that does the same thing at lower cost (a parameter, a MAY, a negotiated extension) set
  to it. It never turns a capability off and never leaves what the RFCs permit; a cheaper
  libwebrtc value that lies outside an RFC belongs to `Chrome`, not here. Each value is
  measured: section 1a.

```rust
let profile = BehaviourProfile::Chrome;
let setting_engine = SettingEngineBuilder::new().with_behaviour_profile(profile).build();
let mut media_engine = MediaEngine::for_profile(profile);
media_engine.register_default_codecs()?;
// Reads the media engine's profile:
let registry = register_default_interceptors(Registry::new(), &mut media_engine)?;
```

A setting given after `with_behaviour_profile` keeps its own value. The connection's
automatic RTCP session (a registry without one) follows the setting engine's profile.

## The `chrome-defaults` cargo feature

With the `chrome-defaults` feature of the `rtci` crate, `BehaviourProfile::default()` is
`Chrome`, and so is every `SettingEngine::default()`, `SettingEngineBuilder::new()`,
`MediaEngine::default()` and `DefaultInterceptorOptions::default()`.

**Cargo unifies features across a dependency graph: one crate of a build that enables
`chrome-defaults` changes the defaults of every user of `rtci` in that build**, libraries
that never asked for it included. Prefer the explicit `with_behaviour_profile` call;
`BehaviourProfile::compiled_default()` tells which default a build has.

## The `performance-defaults` cargo feature

The same for `Performance`: with the `performance-defaults` feature every default above
is `Performance`. With both features on, `chrome-defaults` wins (it is the one that
changes the wire to match a peer) and the build prints a deprecation warning naming the
two features, so the pick is never silent.

## 1a. What `Performance` changes, and what it was measured to save (5)

Each row: the RFC clause that permits the value, the saving and the cost, measured by
`tests/rtcp_rate_trace_rtc2rtc.rs` (two `rtci` peer connections, virtual time, 20 ms
each way; run with `-- --ignored --nocapture`) and the interceptor tests named.

| Behaviour | `Rfc` | `Performance` | Why it is within the RFCs, saving, cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rtcp.t-rr-interval` | `0ns` | `1s` | RFC 4585 3.4 (m): T_rr_interval is "an OPTIONAL minimal interval" between Regular RTCP packets, set by the application; 3.5.3 suppresses regular packets inside it and holds no feedback; RFC 5506 3.3 names trr-int as the remedy for regular reports "of higher density" than needed. Kept local, not announced as a=rtcp-fb:* trr-int: it states only this endpoint's own minimum (RFC 4585 4.2), and no browser fixture carries the line. Measured (tests/rtcp_rate_trace_rtc2rtc.rs, 30 s, a=rtcp-rsize): 1 Mbit/s one way, sender 13.2 -> 1.4 regular packets/s, 27.3 -> 3.8 SR/s, RTCP 4.20% -> 1.45% of the media; both ways 19.4 -> 1.5 regular/s, 4.91% -> 1.44%; without rsize both ways 5.03% -> 2.25%. Cost: report blocks to the sender (RTT from LSR/DLSR, RR loss, the RTP circuit breaker's input) 12.2/s -> 1.2/s, longest gap 214 ms -> 1.36 s; the breaker counts its windows in reports (MEDIA_TIMEOUT 5, CB_INTERVAL at least 3), so it reacts in seconds instead of under one. Unchanged: the NACK (120 ms -> 114-120 ms from loss to request), the congestion control feedback (20/s, 50 ms apart), and Gcc's loss and RTT, which come from that feedback whenever transport-cc or RFC 8888 is negotiated |
| `rtcp.congestion-feedback-in-budget` | `false` | `true` | RFC 3550 6.2: RTCP, feedback included, is 5% of the session bandwidth; the regular interval computed with what the congestion control feedback (sent and received, last 2 s) leaves is applied as a T_rr_interval (RFC 4585 3.5.3: suppression only), at most 5 s (RFC 4585 5). Measured with the next three rows, 30 s, a=rtcp-rsize: 24 kbit/s audio (38.5 kbit/s on the wire) RTCP 12.15% -> 4.49% of the media, without rsize 14.34% -> 6.06% (the minimal compound around each feedback packet is larger than the cadence counts); 100 kbit/s audio and video (203 kbit/s on the wire) 5.96% -> 2.75%. Cost: at 24 kbit/s one regular report every 5 s (report blocks 1.9/s -> 0.2/s, longest gap 657 ms -> 5.2 s); the circuit breaker's RTCP timeout (3 Td, Td at most 5 s) still holds. With RED on audio by default (RFC 2198, train 11) the 24 kbit/s call is 64.5 kbit/s on the wire: 7.46% -> 3.57% |
| `rtcp.minimum-session-bandwidth` | `64000` | `16000` | RFC 3550 6.2 takes the session bandwidth as what the session expects; the media measured both ways is used down to 16 kbit/s instead of 64 kbit/s, so a 24 kbit/s call's RTCP is 5% of 24 kbit/s, not of 64. Alone (rtci-interceptor tests/rtcp_session_timing.rs::the_minimum_session_bandwidth_lets_rtcp_follow_low_media): a 27 kbit/s sender sends 0.3 to 0.6 times the default's regular reports. In the profile it sizes the budget of rtcp.congestion-feedback-in-budget |
| `cc.feedback-share` | `0.05` | `0.025` | RFC 8888 4 leaves the interval to "the acceptable feedback overhead"; half of the 5% goes to the feedback, the rest to the reports. Measured: 100 kbit/s audio and video 12.2 -> 4.3 feedback packets/s (longest gap 137 -> 399 ms); 24 kbit/s audio 4.0 -> 2.0/s (250 -> 500 ms); 1 Mbit/s unchanged (20/s, the 50 ms floor). Cost (rtci-interceptor tests/gcc_feedback_rate.rs, 500 ms against 250 ms): Gcc settles in 0.5 s either way on a 150 kbit/s path, 6.0 s against 5.5 s on a 500 kbit/s one; a Gcc sender with probing fed by a Performance receiver reaches 2 Mbit/s from 300 kbit/s in 0.62 s (default 0.49 s; tests/congestion_feedback_rate.rs::a_gcc_sender_fed_by_a_performance_receiver_ramps_within_a_second) |
| `cc.feedback-max-interval` | `250ms` | `500ms` | draft-holmer-rmcat-transport-wide-cc-extensions-01 3: "in cases of low uplink bandwidth it is acceptable to send them less frequently, e.g., for instance once per RTT"; RFC 8888 4 sets no bound (its 50-200 ms is a measured range of some algorithms, not a requirement). Takes effect only below about 270 kbit/s of media (where 2.5% no longer holds a packet in 250 ms); figures and cost with cc.feedback-share |

Other overhead the trace showed, left as it is because `Performance` already covers it
or no RFC-permitted setting changes it:

- The start-up value of the session bandwidth (1 Mbit/s with video, 64 kbit/s with audio,
  for the first two seconds of media): 13.5 to 14.5 regular packets/s in those two seconds
  against 2.5/s after them at 100 kbit/s. Under `Performance` `T_rr_interval` holds them
  to about one a second; no setting of its own.
- The peer's reduced-size feedback pulls `avg_rtcp_size` down (RFC 5506 3.4 expects it),
  so regular reports speed up: 19.4 regular packets/s each way at 1 Mbit/s both ways
  with `a=rtcp-rsize`, 15.9/s without. Under `Performance` 1.5 and 1.4/s.
- Not in `Performance` because they are outside an RFC: libwebrtc's 5 s audio report
  interval whatever the bandwidth (section 3) and congestion control feedback outside
  the RTCP bandwidth (`rtcp.immediate-congestion-feedback`, the engine's default too, an
  audit row for the owner).

## 2. Engine-only capabilities: the same in every profile (27)

A capability the engine has and Chrome lacks stays on under `Chrome`: it negotiates
down with a Chrome peer, or a Chrome peer does not notice it. Further engine-only
capabilities with no setting: RFC 7728 pause / resume, SFrame, Cryptex negotiation
(libwebrtc's `cryptex_policy` is `kDisabled` by default), receive simulcast with
`a=imageattr`, several transports and BUNDLE groups, RTCP extended reports, and the
statistics the engine reports beyond Chrome's. DTLS 1.3 with DTLS 1.2 fallback is
not engine-only: libwebrtc offers it too (`PeerConnectionFactoryInterface::Options`
`ssl_max_version = SSL_PROTOCOL_DTLS_13`, `api/peer_connection_interface.h`, which
Chromium leaves), and Chromium adds the X25519MLKEM768 key share under its
`kWebRtcPqcForDtls` feature, as the engine does where its crypto backend has it.

| Setting | Note |
|---|---|
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_sctp_message_interleaving` | RFC 8260 I-DATA announced; libwebrtc announces it only under the WebRTC-DataChannelMessageInterleaving field trial (media/sctp/dcsctp_transport.cc::CreateDcSctpOptions @ a222406d), off by default, so it negotiates down to DATA chunks |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_sctp_path_mtu_discovery` | RFC 8899 PLPMTUD probes (HEARTBEAT + PAD); a peer without it answers the HEARTBEAT and nothing else changes |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_sctp_zero_checksum` | RFC 9653 zero checksum, used only when the peer announces it too; dcsctp has it but libwebrtc leaves zero_checksum_alternate_error_detection_method at None (net/dcsctp/public/dcsctp_options.h @ a222406d), so it announces none |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_sctp_weighted_fair_queueing` | RFC 8260 3.6 scheduling of the engine's own sends; not visible to the peer |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_disable_sdp_tls_id` | a=tls-id (RFC 8842) is written; libwebrtc writes and reads none (api/webrtc_sdp.cc @ a222406d has no tls-id) |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_tcp_candidate_gathering` | engine-run ICE-TCP; the train's Chromium gathered no TCP candidate (matrix: "ICE-TCP" cells na-browser) |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_tcp_simultaneous_open` | RFC 6544 S-O candidates; libwebrtc gathers none and connects to one as to a passive candidate |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_tcp_close_unused_connections` | RFC 6544 8 housekeeping of the engine's own ICE-TCP connections |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_turn_over_streams` | engine-run TURN over TCP / TLS |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_turn_tcp_relay` | RFC 6062 TCP allocations; libwebrtc makes none |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_server_reflexive_gathering` | who gathers server-reflexive candidates (engine or application); a sans-I/O choice |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_relay_gathering` | who gathers relayed candidates (engine or application); a sans-I/O choice |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_ecn` | ECN needs the application's socket layer; off in every profile (the ECN rows above apply when it is on) |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_srtp_automatic_rekeying` | RFC 5764 4.4 re-keying by a new association; libwebrtc has none, and a browser peer ignores the new tls-id |

| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_video_receive_limits` | a=imageattr (RFC 6236); none by default in every profile, Chromium writes none |

| `MediaEngine::set_header_extension_encryption` | RFC 6904 encrypted header extensions offered beside the clear ones; libwebrtc's CryptoOptions has them on (api/crypto/crypto_options.h @ a222406d) but Chromium turns them on only with the kWebRtcEncryptedRtpHeaderExtensions feature (rtc_peer_connection_handler.cc @ Chromium 8dafa8bc), and takes the clear ones |
| `DefaultInterceptorOptions::congestion_feedback` | RFC 8888 (ack ccfb) offered beside transport-cc; libwebrtc offers and accepts it only under the WebRTC-RFC8888CongestionControlFeedback field trial (pc/media_session.cc::OfferRfc8888 @ a222406d), so Chromium answers transport-cc |

| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_cryptex_required_on_every_bundled_section` | off: a BUNDLE group's Cryptex is read from its tagged section (RFC 8859 TRANSPORT, RFC 9143 7.1.3); `true` is the JSEP stack's earlier strict reading, in no profile. libwebrtc reads it from the group's first RTP section too: pc/jsep_transport_controller.cc::BundleUsesCryptex @ a222406d (lines 80-90), used for jsep_description.transport_desc.cryptex (lines 918-921); Chromium's cryptex_policy is kDisabled by default |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_dtls_new_association_on_previous_addresses` | off in every profile: a new DTLS association over UDP gets a new 3-tuple (RFC 8842 5.1 MUST, 6), so the ICE restart that comes with it drops the local candidates and refuses their addresses, the TURN links allocate again, and the transport set up again after every m= section was rejected gathers on new ports too; `true` is the opt-out for an application with one fixed socket, in no profile. libwebrtc gathers each ICE generation on new sockets as well: p2p/base/p2p_transport_channel.cc::P2PTransportChannel::MaybeStartGathering @ a222406d (lines 842-882) stops the previous allocator session and takes a pooled or new one, and p2p/client/basic_port_allocator.cc binds that session's UDP sockets afresh (AllocationSequence::Init, lines 1261-1266, with the shared socket; AllocationSequence::CreateUDPPorts, lines 1471-1481, without it), port 0 within min_port..max_port |
| `DefaultInterceptorOptions::nack_retransmission_rate_limit` | the same in every profile: the engine default (UpToTarget on master, the measured choice in tests/capacity_cap_video_rtc2rtc.rs; WithinTarget, RFC 4588 7, once conf/gcc-2-rfc-retransmission lands). libwebrtc has no retransmission rate limit on video at a222406d: call/rtp_video_sender.cc (lines 292-354) configures no retransmission_rate_limiter, which modules/rtp_rtcp/source/rtp_rtcp_interface.h line 92 defaults to nullptr, so RTPSender::ReSendPacket's TryUseRate check (rtp_sender.cc lines 331-333) never applies; instead modules/video_coding/fec_controller_default.cc (lines 146-167) lowers the encoder target by the share NACK and FEC took, capped at kProtectionOverheadRateThreshold 0.5 (line 31). That is the RFC's form (retransmissions inside the target, the originals lowered to make room) closer than UpToTarget, which is not libwebrtc's rule at this revision; Performance keeps the default (UpToTarget measured worse than WithinTarget on the paced default chain by gcc-2's owner) |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_audio_redundancy` | WhenPreferred in every profile: a local audio stream is sent in RED (RFC 2198) only when the remote description lists RED ahead of the primary (RFC 3264 5.1, 6.1). libwebrtc the same: media/engine/webrtc_voice_engine.cc::WebRtcVoiceSendChannel::SetSendCodecs @ a222406d (lines 1507-1641) looks for RED only among the codecs before the send codec (lines 1610-1622: "RED codec needs to be negotiated before the actual codec they reference", for (i = 0; i < send_codec_position; ++i)) |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_own_payload_types_in_answers` | off: an answer uses the offer's payload type numbers (RFC 3264 6.1 SHOULD). libwebrtc the same: pc/codec_vendor.cc::NegotiateCodecs @ a222406d (lines 801-...) "Use their ID, if available" (lines 846-848: negotiated.id = theirs->id), apt values remapped after (lines 853-) |

| Setting | Note |
|---|---|
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_ice_pacing_group` | a budget shared between the application's peer connections |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_crypto_provider` | the cryptographic provider |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_turn_allocation_refresh_interval_cap` | a NAT keep-alive need of the deployment |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_host_acceptance_min_wait` | nomination wait for host pairs |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_srflx_acceptance_min_wait` | nomination wait for server-reflexive pairs |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_prflx_acceptance_min_wait` | nomination wait for peer-reflexive pairs |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_relay_acceptance_min_wait` | nomination wait for relayed pairs |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_network_types` | which networks the application gathers on |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_nat_1to1_ips` | the deployment's public addresses |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_multicast_dns_timeout` | mDNS query timeout |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_multicast_dns_local_name` | a fixed mDNS name |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_multicast_dns_local_ip` | the mDNS answer address |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_multicast_dns_destination_reported` | what the application's socket layer reports |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_multicast_dns_unicast_response` | depends on the application's socket being the only one on port 5353 |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_multicast_dns_rate_limit` | a limit shared between the application's peer connections |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_discard_local_candidates_during_ice_restart` | whether the application's sockets outlive an ICE restart |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_ice_credentials` | fixed credentials for tests |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_ice_tie_breaker` | a fixed tiebreaker for tests |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_remote_address_filter` | the host's network policy |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_dtls_replay_protection_window` | replay window |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_srtp_replay_protection_window` | replay window |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_srtcp_replay_protection_window` | replay window |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_mid_generator` | the application's mid naming |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_sctp_max_receive_buffer_size` | memory per connection |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_sctp_mtu` | a known path budget (fixing it turns path MTU discovery off) |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_stream_limits` | limits of the engine's stream transports |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_turn_tls` | roots or a verifier for TURN over TLS |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_behaviour_profile` | the profile itself |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::without_sctp_rto` | back to the RFC 9260 timers (the sctp.rto row's Rfc value) |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::without_sctp_max_retransmissions` | back to RFC 9260's 10 (the sctp.max-retransmissions row's Rfc value) |
| `DefaultInterceptorOptions::rtcp_random` | an injected random source for the RTCP sessions (report interval variation, RFC 3550 6.3.1; early feedback dither, RFC 4585 3.5.2; SSRC and CNAME), for runs a seeded provider makes repeatable; `None` (rand) in every profile |
| `DefaultInterceptorOptions::wall_clock` | an injected wall-clock anchor for the NTP times the interceptors write (sender reports, XR receiver reference times, RFC 8888 report timestamps, the RFC 6051 header extension), for virtual-time runs that repeat within one process; `None` (the process-wide SystemInstant::shared) in every profile |
| `SettingEngineBuilder::with_wall_clock` | an injected wall-clock time for the instant the peer connection is built at, for the wall-clock values it writes itself (the o= session version, RFC 8866 5.2; the receivers' source timestamps; the NTP times of the RTCP session it installs), for virtual-time runs that repeat; `None` (the system clock, read once) in every profile |

## 3. Not expressible (12)

What Chrome does that no setting of the engine can express, and what it would take.

| Behaviour | Chrome | What would be needed |
|---|---|---|
| NACK request limits counted in packets | modules/video_coding/nack_requester.cc @ a222406d: a missing packet more than kMaxPacketAge 10,000 sequence numbers behind the newest is no longer asked for (lines 34, 210-211), and a NACK list that would pass kMaxNackPackets 1000 entries is cleared and a key frame requested instead (lines 35, 214-219). kMaxPacketAgeToNack 450 in video/rtp_video_stream_receiver2.cc (line 114) is not a NACK limit: it is the receive statistics' reordering threshold (SetMaxReorderingThreshold, lines 337-340) | limits in sequence numbers in NackGeneratorBuilder: its with_max_packet_age is a time (Duration), not a packet count, and no setting clears the list for a key frame. Both profiles keep no age limit (RFC 4588 6.3 gives none) |
| ICE connectivity check retransmission | no retransmission: each check is sent once and given kConnectionResponseTimeout 60 s (p2p/base/connection.cc::ConnectionRequest::OnSent / resend_delay @ a222406d); the channel sends a new check every kWeakPingInterval 48 ms while no pair is writable, a pair with no answer being unreliable after 5 checks and 5 s (Connection::UpdateState). Only requests to STUN / TURN servers retransmit: STUN_INITIAL_RTO 250 ms doubling to STUN_MAX_RTO 8 s, 9 sends (p2p/base/stun_request.cc) | a check scheduler in rtci-ice that replaces transactions by new checks; the engine's checks are RFC 8489 transactions with RTO at least 500 ms (RFC 8445 14.3, a MUST: "RTO = MAX (500ms, ...)") |
| Consent / keepalive pings on the selected pair | every kStrongAndStableWritableConnectionPingInterval 2.5 s on a strong, stable connection, 900 ms while it stabilises, 480 ms strong / 48 ms weak at the channel level (p2p/base/p2p_constants.h @ a222406d) | nothing that keeps RFC 7675 5.1: a period under 4 s is forbidden (MUST NOT), the engine raises it to 5 s |
| Candidate type preferences | host 126, prflx 110, srflx 100, host TCP 90, prflx TCP 80, relayed UDP 3 / TCP 1 / TLS 0 (p2p/base/p2p_constants.h IcePriorityValue @ a222406d) | a candidate-priority policy in rtci-ice; the engine takes RFC 8445 5.1.2.2's (host 126, prflx 110, srflx 100, relayed 0) and for TCP the UDP preference less one (RFC 6544 4.2) |
| Payload type numbering and codec order | Chromium's numbering (opus 111, red 63, VP8 96, VP9 98 / 100, AV1 45, H264 102...; fixtures) | a Chrome codec table; the application registers its own codecs with MediaEngine::register_codec. Payload types are negotiated, so this changes no behaviour |
| Header extensions the engine does not implement | toffset, playout-delay, video-content-type, video-timing, color-space (fixtures) | an implementation of each; offering them without one would announce what the engine does not send |
| RTCP report interval per media type | 5 s for audio, 1 s for video, and for video sent above 72 kbit/s min(360 s / kbit/s, 1 s), drawn from [0.5, 1.5] of it (modules/rtp_rtcp/source/rtp_rtcp_impl2.cc, rtcp_sender.cc::RTCPSender::ComputeTimeUntilNextReport @ a222406d) | a per-kind interval in the RTCP session; the Chrome profile sets T_rr to 1 s for every section |
| Transports of an initial offer | every section in one BUNDLE group whatever the bundle policy, max-compat included (pc/sdp_offer_answer.cc: bundle_enabled = use_rtp_mux; pc/media_session.cc::UpdateTransportInfoForBundle @ a222406d): one ice-ufrag in all sections, candidates for the first transport only | a bundle layout setting; the engine gives each media type a transport of its own under balanced and every section one under max-compat (RFC 9429 4.1.1), each with credentials of its own under Chrome's per-transport rule (sdp.unique-transport-credentials) |
| Candidate generation / network-id / network-cost | a=candidate lines end with generation <n>, and network-id <n> / network-cost <n> where the network is known (api/candidate.cc::BuildCandidate @ a222406d; fixtures: generation 0 network-cost 999) | nothing cheap and harmless: network-id and network-cost are the application socket layer's knowledge of its interfaces, and a made-up cost would change libwebrtc's choice of pair (basic_ice_controller.cc::CompareCandidatePairNetworks prefers the lower cost); generation is redundant, since libwebrtc reads the ufrag the engine writes before it (p2p_transport_channel.cc::GetRemoteCandidateGeneration) |
| Google STUN attributes in connectivity checks | GOOG-NETWORK-INFO in every check, GOOG-MISC-INFO / GOOG_PING, GOOG-DELTA and DTLS-in-STUN behind field trials (p2p/base/connection.cc::Connection::BuildPingRequest @ a222406d) | an implementation of libwebrtc's private attributes (comprehension-optional, RFC 8489 14: a peer without them ignores them) |
| Delay-based estimator filter | a trendline filter: window 20, smoothing 0.9, threshold gain 4, adaptive threshold gains k_up 0.0087 (outside) / k_down 0.039 (inside) (modules/congestion_controller/goog_cc/trendline_estimator.cc / .h @ a222406d) | a trendline estimator in rtci-interceptor; the engine's adaptive threshold takes draft-ietf-rmcat-gcc-02 5.4's gains, K_u 0.01 / K_d 0.00018 |
| SCTP INIT retransmissions | unlimited (max_init_retransmits none, media/sctp/dcsctp_transport.cc::CreateDcSctpOptions @ a222406d) | a Max.Init.Retransmits setting on the setting engine; the engine keeps RFC 9260's 8 |

## How it is checked

- `src/peer_connection/configuration/behaviour_profile_test.rs`: every value of every
  profile, the `Rfc` column against the engine's own defaults, a peer connection built the
  default way under each profile (its ICE agent configuration included), and that every
  setting of `SettingEngineBuilder`, `MediaEngine` and `DefaultInterceptorOptions` is in
  this document (a new setting without a profile entry fails the test and this script).
- `tests/behaviour_profiles.rs`: under `Chrome`, an offer and an answer compared
  structurally with the committed Chromium descriptions (the engine's extra attributes are
  listed there as documented differences); rtc to rtc connections with data and media
  between profiles, and the `StrictRfc` refusals.
- `scripts/behaviour-profiles.py --check` (a Python gate of `cargo.yml`): this document is
  what the code says.
- The browser matrix runs the core scenarios with the Rust peer under `Chrome`
  (`examples/interop-peer`, `profile=chrome`).
